results.title: 3D Bounding Box Packing
results.prompt: Can 12 rectangular boxes of dimensions 2x3x4 be packed into a container of dimensions 6x6x8 without overlap? Provide the volume check and geometric proof.
results.reply: The volume check shows that the total volume of the twelve boxes is exactly 288 cubic units, which matches the total volume of the container. To prove they can be packed without overlap, we can use a simple tiling strategy where we stack the boxes in layers. Since each box has a height of 4 and the container has a height of 8, we can create two horizontal layers of 6x6x4. In each layer, we arrange six 2x3x4 boxes by placing them such that their 2x3 faces form a grid on the 6x6 base. Specifically, three boxes side-by-side along one 6-unit edge and two rows of those would perfectly fill the 6x6 area. Since both layers fit perfectly, all twelve boxes will fit into the container without any gaps or overlaps.
